transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-15
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (AE - Redwood), Priya (SE - Redwood), Liam (PMM - Redwood), Alex (Head of ML - Apex Insights), Maya (Product), Diego (Eng Lead)

Summary:
Quick internal SE enablement on updated messaging, competitive positioning, and demo practice tailored for Apex Insights POC. Walkthrough of key objections and a 15-minute demo run to practice handoffs. Agreed next steps: share deck, schedule mock demo, run PII benchmark.

[00:00] Jordan (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining on a friday afternoon, appreciate it. quick check, audio ok?
[00:07] Priya (SE): yep, loud and clear. thanks Jordan. we'll keep this tight, about an hour, 30 mins messaging, 20 demo practice, then q&a.
[00:20] Liam (PMM): hi, small note — updated one-pager in the slide deck, called out quantization and dedicated vs hosted messaging.
[00:30] Alex (Customer): great, can you also call out data residency and encryption, that's a key gate for us.
[00:36] Jordan: totally. we'll make sure SOC2/SAML/KMS are front and center, and also mention the private deployment option for apex legal.

Topics: positioning vs OpenAI/Anthropic, Dedicated vs Hosted messaging, demo script for PII redaction use-case, objection handling for latency/cost, security checklist.

[02:10] Priya: ok starting with the 2-slide elevator — 1) what redwood does: unified runtime to run and optimize LLM inference across hosted, dedicated and private. 2) Why that matters: predictable latency and cost controls for production apps. i'm gonna read it, let me know if phrasing feels salesy.
[02:25] Jordan: sounds good, maybe replace "predictable latency" with "SLA-backed latency guarantees" for enterprise calls, since that's often the ask.
[02:33] Priya: good call, SLA-backed. also call out that we do auto fallback to model variants to avoid outages.
[02:39] Liam: add a short bullet on caching and KV cache to justify cost improvements — customers care about token economics.

[04:00] Alex: quick interruption — for our side, the big three are: security/compliance, predictable cost at scale, and easy rollout to our private cloud. 
[04:10] Jordan: understood. we'll map those directly to features: SOC2/ISO + VPC/private, batching/quantization suggestions via Redwood Optimize, and the private deployment option.

Competitive framing section:
[05:02] Priya: when customers ask about OpenAI — messaging should be: OpenAI is great for quick experimentation, but Redwood focuses on production economics, control, and hybrid deployment. for Anthropic, highlight that Redwood offers more deployment flexibility and observability hooks — per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdowns.
[05:30] Jordan: add a line on model catalog and verified performance profiles; customers sometimes assume we only do in-house models.
[05:38] Liam: also call out that we integrate with KMS/HSM for key management, which is a differentiate vs some hosted-only vendors.

Objections practice:
[07:10] Diego (playing devil's advocate): cost — our CFO will ask why not just use XYZ cloud provider endpoints, cheaper with spot GPUs.
[07:22] Priya: good objection — response: we show TCO per 1M requests with and without batching/caching; Redwood Optimize can reduce per-token unit costs materially and our reserved Dedicated option offers predictable throughput vs spot. plus, hidden costs of engineering and ops to build comparable routing/rollback capabilities.
[07:45] Jordan: also mention SLO-backed uptime and automatic fallbacks; outages on commodity endpoints often cost more than savings.

Security and compliance role-play:
[09:00] Alex: our security team will push back on data in third-party clouds.
[09:05] Priya: recommended reply — we offer Private deployment (VPC and on-prem) and customer-managed control plane, full audit logs, and KMS integrations. show the SOC2/ISO doc and the architecture diagram.
[09:20] Jordan: action: attach compliance pack to the deal email.

Demo practice setup:
[10:05] Priya: ok demo — target: PII redaction flow in a customer ticketing pipeline. keep it customer-centric: show latency, model selection, and how caching reduces cost. we'll run 10-12 minutes, Jordan will do the product framing and hand off to me for the technical deep dive.
[10:30] Jordan: sound good. i'll open with the "why Redwood" slide and call out the three things apex cares about.

Demo run — live practice (this is intentionally imperfect to simulate real world)
[12:00] Priya: starting demo — showing Redwood Console, per-route dashboard, token-level cost graph. note: in the console mock we have a sample called "apex-pii-redact".
[12:22] Alex: looks nice, can you show the model variant fallback?
[12:28] Priya: sure, switching to the routing tab — you can set policy: region -> dedicated -> hosted fallback. (mumbled) sometimes the UI label is "fallback policy" in the alpha.
[12:45] Jordan: small improv: when Alex asks about throughput, call out that Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools and autoscaling policies.
[13:10] Priya: switching engines — demonstrating KV/prefix caching: here's a 10k token prefix that gets cached, subsequent requests are faster and cheaper.
[13:40] Diego: what's the expected latency at 500 req/s?
[13:45] Priya: approximate numbers: on Dedicated n1 GPUs we see p95 around 120-180ms for short requests; depends a lot on model family and quantization. note: these numbers are for internal decks — we'll run a benchmark for apex numbers.
[14:05] Alex: are those numbers against FP16? what about int8 quant?
[14:12] Priya: FP16 vs int8 can give 1.5-2x perf improvement; we recommend model/quantization profiles per workload. again, we'll provide a benchmark sheet.

[16:00] Jordan: ok small break in demo — let's roleplay a tricky interruption: customer asks about model outputs quality after quantization. Priya?
[16:10] Priya: answer: quantization-friendly execution paths preserve accuracy for most LLM tasks; we tie quality monitoring and regression alerts to prompt sets and evals — so any drop is flagged. we can also route critical requests to FP16 model variants.
[16:40] Alex: good to hear. how do you handle KV cache invalidation for dynamic content?
[16:48] Priya: cache keys include prefix and user session; we expose TTLs and manual invalidation APIs.

Demo awkward moment / transcript artifacts:
[19:00] Priya: (typing noises) uh, sorry slowness on my end — i'm on a demo VM that's a little noisy, ignore the stutter.
[19:10] Jordan: that's realistic though, mention that demo envs can differ and always caveat with "production numbers may vary".

Practice wrap and feedback:
[24:00] Liam: quick feedback — Jordan, your handoffs are smooth, callouts to SLA could be earlier; Priya, try to shorten deep technical dives to 90 seconds unless customer asks.
[24:30] Alex: for apex specifically, please publish a short checklist for our security review (SSO, KMS, data flows).
[24:40] Jordan: noted — i'll include that in the pack.

Open Qs and risky objections noted:
[26:00] Diego: procurement will challenge long-term lock-in; how do we answer renewals vs model changes?
[26:10] Jordan: response: emphasize ability to pin model versions and rollouts, can do canary/A-B and automatic rollback. plus, migration support during renewals. also transparent pricing for switching models.

Closing and recap:
[29:00] Jordan: recap — items: share updated deck and competitor one-pager (Jordan), Priya to coordinate mock demo and run benchmarks, attach compliance docs (Liam). agreed target dates over the next 10 days.
[29:20] Alex: sounds good, looking forward to the mock demo.
[29:25] Maya: thanks team.

End of call.

References/Shared artifacts mentioned:
- SE messaging deck (link: internal_drive/redwood/se_deck_v2.pdf)
- Competitor one-pager (link: internal_drive/redwood/competitor_matrix.xlsx)
- Compliance pack (link: internal_drive/redwood/compliance/soc2_package.pdf)

Notes on transcription quality: a few stutters and mislabeled UI names (e.g., "fallback policy" vs "fallback rule"), speaker overlaps at the demo handoff, some numbers approximate.
